The broad intervals concern the city before the crisis, while surface repair and robot fighting remain visible external labor rather than evidence of universal leisure.

after.analysis:
Leisureland lets some miniaturized people turn savings into an affluent lifestyle because small bodies consume fewer physical resources. Poor miniature residents and human service work remain visible. That is a real material change and a useful comparison, but its established mechanism is reduced consumption and purchasing advantage rather than automatic production. The earlier omission is therefore replaced by a completed assessment instead of a demand for deeper lore reading.

 The coordinate scenario gives the combined miniature community weak guarantees, partly dispersed private human control and a moderate nonworking share. Affluent leisure cannot stand for the poor residents or service workers. These are broad editorial estimates, not claims that shrinking creates universal rights or eliminates useful work. The comparison stays outside the target because the known productivity mechanism differs from automation, not because household details are missing. No percentage is inferred from body size, money multiplication or the existence of a wealthy protagonist.
